title: MSSQLSERVER on windows: compound failure — bad_config + missing_permission
scenario: A production MSSQLSERVER (db) on windows will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: a syntax error was introduced in the main config file AND the runtime user cannot read a required file/dir. a config edit also changed file ownership, so fixing syntax alone still fails on permissions. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'bad_config' and 'missing_permission' on MSSQLSERVER
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `MSSQLSERVER` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.

Read the evidence fully: `Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 120 | Where-Object Message -match 'MSSQLSERVER'` shows TWO distinct signals ('configuration file test failed' and 'Permission denied').
Interaction: a config edit also changed file ownership, so fixing syntax alone still fails on permissions.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'bad_config': run the config validator to locate the error; correct the offending directive.
Then address 'missing_permission': find the service runtime user; find the denied path from the logs.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `MSSQLSERVER` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 1433 if applicable) with BOTH 'bad_config' and 'missing_permission' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Keep a copy of the original config; if the edit is wrong, restore it and re-derive the fix from the validator output. Ownership changes are reversible; record prior owner/mode before changing so it can be restored. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: a config edit also changed file ownership, so fixing syntax alone still fails on permissions

possible_mistakes: overwrite the config from memory instead of fixing one line
chmod 777 the whole tree instead of the one path
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: a config edit also changed file ownership, so fixing syntax alone still fails on permissions.
reference_solution: Observe both signals: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 120 | Where-Object Message -match 'MSSQLSERVER'
Resolve 'bad_config' first: run the config validator to locate the error; correct the offending directive
Then resolve 'missing_permission': find the service runtime user; find the denied path from the logs
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio MSSQLSERVER non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (bad_config e missing_permission). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
